findings.title: All-groups VIEW permission grants manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() treats a permission that only includes the VIEW scope as sufficient to manage groups: hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) returns true if either scope is granted on the all-groups resource. requireManage() (used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup and other write paths) therefore allows an admin who was only granted view-all-groups to create and otherwise manage groups. canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE; the no-arg method should do the same and must not accept VIEW.

findings.title: View-members group filter uses authz resource ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is what UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource put into the UserModel.GROUPS search attribute so user queries are limited to groups the caller may view. The callback adds groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource id) and also passes that id into hasPermission(), which looks the resource up by name. V2 group resources are named with the group id (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), so the lookup misses the real resource and the returned set is not a set of group ids. User search/count then either drops members the caller is allowed to see or filters on ids that match no group. It should evaluate and return the resource name (the group id), and skip the all-groups type resource whose name is "Groups". Individual group resources created in getOrCreateResource also never have their type set to Groups, so findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) will not see them at all.

findings.title: Group resources are not resolved to a display name
findings.body: getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group permission resources are stored under the group id as the name and are not given a display name in getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup. Admin permission UIs that call getResourceName for a Groups policy therefore show a blank name (or fail later if a non-null label is assumed) instead of the group name or path, the same way users are resolved to a username.
